sentences.l2: 阅读经济新闻时，读者常被“同比增长”“环比增长”这类表述搞得眼花缭乱。
sentences.l1: When reading economic news, readers are often dazzled by expressions like "year-on-year growth" and "month-on-month growth."

sentences.l2: 同比，是把本期数据与去年同一时期相比，可以剔除季节性波动的干扰；环比，则是与紧邻的上一个时期相比，更能反映短期的变化趋势。
sentences.l1: Year-on-year is comparing the current period's data with the same period of last year, which can remove the interference of seasonal fluctuations; month-on-month, by contrast, is comparing with the immediately preceding period, and better reflects short-term trends.

sentences.l2: 以某国季度GDP为例，若第二季度同比增长5%，说明经济总量高于上年同期；若环比仅增长0.3%，则意味着相较第一季度，增速已明显放缓。
sentences.l1: Taking a certain country's quarterly GDP as an example, if the second quarter grows 5% year-on-year, it shows that the economic total is higher than in the same period of the previous year; if it grows only 0.3% month-on-month, it means that compared with the first quarter, the growth rate has clearly slowed.

sentences.l2: 还须留意基数效应：假如去年同期受到冲击，数值偏低，今年的增长率即便亮眼，也可能只是低基数带来的“虚高”；反之，高基数会使增长率显得平淡。
sentences.l1: One must also pay attention to the base effect: if the same period last year was hit by a shock and the value was low, then even if this year's growth rate is impressive, it may only be an "inflated" figure brought by a low base; conversely, a high base will make the growth rate look flat.

sentences.l2: 因此，单看一个增长率容易以偏概全，唯有将同比、环比结合起来，并参考背后的基数，才能对经济走势作出较为客观的判断。
sentences.l1: Therefore, looking at a single growth rate alone easily takes a part for the whole, and only by combining year-on-year and month-on-month and also consulting the underlying base can one make a fairly objective judgment about the economic trend.
